I pray for their deliverance."* This prompts the side quest to collect Loyce Souls in exchange for pieces of the Loyce Set and eventually her soul.

Every time a Loyce Knight soul is returned to her, she says: *"I sense a knight's joyous elation. Kind visitor, please accept my gratitude."* Progressively, the formations of ice blocking the stairs will break the more souls are returned. Once 15 souls have been returned, she states:

Once 50 souls have been collected, the final pieces of ice break, allowing the player to meet her. She sits at the top of the staircase, kneeling in prayer. When spoken to, her dialogue will allude to her sisters, Nashandra, Elana and Nadalia:

title: Alsanna, Silent Oracle
snippet:
Eventually, the Ivory King sensed the degradation of his soul and left Eleum Loyce without a word, leaving everything to Alsanna. Upon his departure, he gifted her an intertwined blade of shadow and light, revealing to her that he had already known about her Dark nature. He traveled deep into the Chaos for one final assault but was eventually devoured by its flames. In a last ditch attempt to quell the fiery Chaos, the Gates of Eleum Loyce were opened, allowing the cold harsh blizzard to consume the kingdom whole.

In spite of all this, Alsanna bravely chose to remain and devoted herself to prayer to appease the raging flame in memory of her loving lord. All the while hoping that despite all odds, he might perhaps one day return.

title: Alsanna, Silent Oracle
snippet:
Alsanna, Silent Oracle -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Alsanna is a mysterious child of the Dark, one of the many fragments of Manus, Father of the Abyss. At an unknown point, she traveled to the northern kingdom of Eleum Loyce, ruled by the Ivory King, and devoted herself to him as his oracle. An ancient Chaos was discovered deep below the land, so in an attempt to appease the raging flame the Ivory King built a great cathedral at its mouth and Alsanna prayed in silent vigilance. The attempt was unsuccessful, and the flames still raged.

title: Anor Londo
snippet:
If the player is killed whilst in darkened Anor Londo, they are returned to the first bonfire regardless of whether they have rested there or not. Whether it is a glitch or an intended function by the developers is unconfirmed.

If the player desires to fight Dark Sun Gwyndolin via an easy return to the boss area, it is preferable to either:
Leave Gwynevere alive so as to not make Anor Londo dark, and then fight Gwyndolin. This allows the player to respawn at the Darkmoon Tomb bonfire.
After killing Gwynevere, ignore the Darkmoon Knightess (so as not to kill her in combat) to keep the first Bonfire lit so that the player may warp to the Darkmoon Tomb after death.

If the player has already darkened Anor Londo and killed the Darkmoon Knightess, the fastest method will be to run to the entrance way of The Duke's Archives (only accessible after placing the Lordvessel) and using the bonfire by the elevator to warp.

 trivia : The Batwing Demon seen at the very beginning of Anor Londo can actually be attacked. Upon attacking, it will flee much like the giant crow in Firelink Shrine. Unlike the crow however, if dealt enough damage the Batwing Demon will indeed die, though it will simply respawn upon resting at a bonfire. Additionally, the "Talk" option used to travel back to Sen's Fortress is still available even if the Batwing Demon has been killed.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : Gargoyles are stone creatures created by the Gods through magic to help patrol Anor Londo or sites deemed important. In addition to their tough and hard skin, they are able to breathe fire or lightning and are armed with a bronze shield and a bronze helmet for purely decorative purposes while they use a bronze halberd as a weapon.

After Lord Gwyn sacrificed himself to link the First Flame and prolong the Age of Fire, several Gargoyles were placed to guard the Bell of Awakening placed on the Undead Church of the Undead Burg and act as ritual challenge. The Undead who wished to follow in Gwyn's footsteps to sacrifice themselves to the Flame would have to be tested before obtaining the Lordvessel and seeking powerful souls. Ringing the Bells of Awakening represents only the first of these challenges, and success means gaining access to Sen's Fortress to be tested further.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - lead 
 lead : The **Bell Gargoyles** (鐘のガーゴイル) are dual bosses in *Dark Souls*.

There are four Gargoyles in the game: the first two are part of the same boss battle atop the Undead Parish, with the second only joining halfway through, while the last two are mini-bosses found in Anor Londo. None of them respawn.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - description 
 description : They appear to be armored gargoyles wielding axes and shields with fire or lightning attacks. They have axes on their tails which they use to swing at you.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - strategy 
 strategy : In human form, it is possible to have Solaire of Astora and/or Knight Lautrec of Carim assist during this battle, although Lautrec must be freed and spoken to in Firelink Shrine first. Their summon signs are found just before the white light leading to the Gargoyles. Summoning both knights and simply mobbing each Gargoyle can lead to a quick and relatively painless victory.

The fight is beset by the constant danger of falling off (target-locking, coupled with the camera angle and narrow field of view, can make it hard to track the player character's footing) and facing off against a single gargoyle on top of the church roof. Trying to circle the gargoyle while holding up a shield is a good way to avoid its long-reaching frontal attacks. If the gargoyle takes off, move away or get ready to dodge its plunging attack.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Bell Gargoyles -  Dark Souls - boss - location 
 location : On top of the church in the Undead Parish, reached by passing through the room full of hollows and a Channeler, before climbing two ladders and finally entering the fog gate. They are also found in Anor Londo as mini-bosses: Exit the first bonfire, go straight on and down the lift, and a gargoyle will be straight ahead. The second is beyond the rotating staircase-bridge.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Once the first gargoyle is cut down to half its health, the second gargoyle will join the fight. Fortunately, this gargoyle is already severely injured (it arrives at half-health). It has the same attacks as the first gargoyle minus those that involve flying or using the tail.

Players having difficulty managing their positioning against the two gargoyles should save any consumables (ex., Fire Bombs) until the first gargoyle's health is approaching 50%, and then use them to finish it off as quickly as possible. For as long as both gargoyles are alive, players should keep them both on the screen; if not feasible, one can try following audio cues to perceive an oncoming attack. The use of Gold Pine Resin and other weapon enhancements can greatly help in finishing off the first gargoyle, and make the overall fight significantly easier.

title: Bell Gargoyles
snippet:
Both Gargoyles wield halberds and can breathe fire, although the first gargoyle usually will only breathe fire after the second one jumps down. A fire-resistant shield such as the Black Knight Shield (and, optionally, fire-resistant armor) can be very useful, as the fire breath covers a wide area. While breathing fire, the gargoyles won't move, making it the perfect opportunity to run over and hit them from behind (this makes avoiding or blocking the fire twice as important, as its stagger effect will consume precious seconds, limiting the time available to attack the gargoyles).

The first gargoyle's tail can be severed to gain a weapon (Gargoyle Tail Axe).

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - quelaag_s_domain_bell 
 quelaag_s_domain_bell : The other Bell is significantly harder to reach. The Chosen Undead must first head downward and find their way into Blighttown, a multileveled and dangerous labyrinth. At the very bottom of Blighttown, the player will traverse a poison swamp leading to a half-demon's lair known as Quelaag's Domain. It is here that the player must defeat Chaos Witch Quelaag in order to progress to the Bell of Awakening.

Upon ringing the second Bell, a short cutscene plays showing the gatekeeper Giant hearing the call and pulling the chains to lift up the portcullis, bearing passage to Sen's Fortress. It is at this point that Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine, and instructs the player that his new task is to secure the Lordvessel, proving that the player is in fact, the Chosen Undead.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bells of Awakening** are a storyline concept, as well as two locations, in *Dark Souls*.

They are the first destinations hinted at for the Chosen Undead after they have escaped the Undead Asylum into Lordran. The two Bells are part of a prophecy devised by the Gods of Anor Londo to help bring about an Undead to link the First Flame. The two Bells are respectively located past the Bell Gargoyles atop the Undead Parish, and past Queelag past the swamp at the bottom of Blighttown. Both Bells must be rung by activating levers near them to progress, opening the way to Sen's Fortress.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - plot 
 plot : The Bells of Awakening are hinted at being the first destination of the Chosen Undead and, when rung, the fate of the undead shall be known. Upon arriving in Firelink Shrine, the Crestfallen Warrior informs the player that there are, in fact, two Bells of Awakening. One up above and one far below. This is essentially all the instruction and plot that is revealed upon arrival in Lordran.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Ringing the bell in Quelaag's Domain first will have no different effect than if the player rang the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] first. Although this will cause Lautrec's questline to progress, leading to the death of Anastacia.
The Bells of Awakening were used to awaken Kingseeker Frampt and open the way to Sen's Fortress.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - notes 
 notes : In the Prepare to Die Edition, online players in the vicinity of the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] were able to hear the bell being rung from other player worlds. This wasn’t the case for the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Bell in Quelaag’s Domain].
In the remastered version of the game, online players are now able to hear either the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] or the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Quelaag’s domain Bell] being rung from other player worlds while exploring one area or the other . (as the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Quelaag’s Bell] toll was specifically added in the remaster)

title: Berenike Knight
snippet:
Berenike Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : Berenike Knights were known for their heavy armor of steel and their ultra-heavy Tower Shields forged with thick plates of iron, favoring hard defense and stability, as well as their gigantic swords capable of causing enormous damage. For their immense strength these knights were extolled as the mightiest of mighty. Among them, Black Iron Tarkus was renowned even among his fellow knights for his great strength; he wore an ultra-heavy armor made of special black iron—one with exceptional fire protection, yet so unwieldy that only he was able to wear it; his greatshield, made of the same fire-resistant material, was even heavier than that of his fellow knights.

title: Berenike Knight

 description : Large and clad in the Steel Set, they wield either a large Mace or Greatsword, depending on the location where they are found, along with a Tower Shield. All Berenike Knights can be parried, but cannot be riposted.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet: As the First Flame began to fade, countless among the ranks of the Berenike Knights became Undead and ventured to Lordran. Here they tried to make their way toward Anor Londo through the only possible access: Sen's Fortress. The knights of Berenike and Tarkus thus entered the dangerous proving ground; after decades of struggling to advance, much of the Knights ended up as Hollows, becoming a threat to the other Undead in the location. Tarkus, probably accompanied by some fellow knights, eventually reached the peak of Sen's Fortress and challenged the last trial in the form of the Iron Golem. The mighty knight in black iron armor managed to defeat the guardian of Anor Londo, gaining access to the city of the gods. However, after reaching Anor Londo, Tarkus perished at the hands of the Painting Guardians before he could reach Gwynevere and obtain the Lordvessel. The few Berenike Knights that followed him to Anor Londo ended up inside the Painted World of Ariamis.

title: Black Eye Orb

Black Eye Orb -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : When in the main chamber before the fight with Dragon Slayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough, the player will receive a notification telling them that the Black Eye Orb is quivering. At this point, the player may invade Lautrec's world to combat him and his two companions, a sorcerer and warrior. If the player successfully kills Lautrec, they are awarded Anastacia's Fire Keeper Soul. Restoring it to Anastacia's cage revives her and re-ignites the Firelink Shrine bonfire. Alternately, it can be consumed for five humanity or used to upgrade Estus Flasks, just like any other Fire Keeper Soul.

Similar to the Blue Eye Orbs, the Black Eye Orb can be used if the player is in Hollow form.

It was designed by [https://www.mobygames.com/person/494904/adam-ledzion/ Adam Ledzion], who appears in the game's credits.
** Its insignia is the symbol of the [https://gestiguiste.net/faqs/ Gestiguiste]. They are an Aratari unit of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dagorhir Dagorhir], a medieval/fantasy combat wargame. This could mean that its designer was part of that group.

 dark_souls : The Painted World was once a peaceful land with kind inhabitants. It hosts a building similar to an old cathedral, whose annex served as a storage house.

The Painted World of Ariamis has much in connection with Velka, Goddess of Sin. Within it, the Black Cleric Robe can be found, said to be given to pardoners serving Velka. Other items attributed to Velka are scattered throughout the area, unique ones that can either be traded or obtained only in the Painted World: Ring of Sacrifice (sacrificial rite to Velka), Velka's Rapier (used by her pardoner), Vow of Silence (her secret rite). The Dark Ember obtained in the Painted World is no longer known to any living blacksmith in the outside world, as it was long hidden by the church.

title: Painted World of Ariamis
snippet:
Painted World of Ariamis -  Dark Souls - location - lore 
 lore : The Painted World of Ariamis, as the name suggests, was created by Ariamis. Painting Guardians were ordered to protect it through generations, however, at some point, the Guardians were not able to recall the reason for doing so.

The Painted World of Ariamis was created as a sanctuary for Crossbreed Priscilla, so that she could be left alone. The key to entering this land is the Peculiar Doll. Once considered an abomination which has no place in this world, Priscilla clutched this doll tightly and was eventually drawn into the lonely, painted world. This abomination was the birth of the Dragon Crossbreed, which is considered a bastard child. She was considered an abomination because the gods of Anor Londo feared her Lifehunt ability, seen as the antithesis of all life and a threat to their immortality.

title: Painted World of Ariamis
snippet:
Painted World of Ariamis -  Dark Souls - location - exiting 
 exiting : Priscilla the Crossbreed, the boss of the area who resides in a tower, will not begin attacking straight away, instead imploring the player to leave her world. Unless the player jumps off the ledge behind Priscilla, it is impossible to leave the Painted World of Ariamis, even with the Lordvessel's warp ability or through the use of a Homeward Bone or the Homeward miracle.

If Priscilla is attacked, attempting to leave by jumping off the ledge will result in death. At this point, players will only be allowed to leave upon her defeat.

title: Ariamis
snippet: Ariamis created the Painted World as a sanctuary for Priscilla, so that she could be left alone. He depicted in his painting a township consisting of a cathedral and a storehouse amidst a wintry forest. Its first inhabitant was Priscilla, a half-dragon that was feared by the gods of Anor Londo and treated as an abomination due to her body being naturally infused with the occult power capable of killing them.

title: Ariamis
snippet:
Ariamis -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Although Ariamis's name and figure were eventually lost to history, their knowledge on the nature of Painted Worlds was passed down. In the following iterations of Paintings, the natives of Painted Worlds possessed a proficient understanding of the First Flame and the Dark Soul. Whenever their world showed signs of corruption, they used the Flame to "restore" the Painting, to avoid the fate of the stagnating outside world. For this purpose the corvians chose a "Father" who presided over the Flame and would burn away their home when the time came. After the Flame was unleashed, a painter like Ariamis would use the Dark Soul as pigment to create a new painting.

title: Painted World of Ariamis
snippet:
Painted World of Ariamis -  Dark Souls - location - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : The Painted World of Ariamis likely rotted and was set on fire in order to be restored. This is a usual cycle within painted worlds. The history of Painted World is no longer known in Lothric. It is taught only in the mythology of heretics, passed down just among them, and in ancient tales of hunchbacked heretics. Those heretics are Corvian Storytellers, spreading tales of Painted World among forlorn ones. They are wretched beings with no place to go, just like their followers, Corvians, the unwanted ones possessed by fear. Some of them wield Great Corvian Scythes, visually resembling the one used by the mistress of the Painted World and causing bleeding. It is a reference to Priscilla's scythe rather than Friede's, mistress of the Painted World of Ariandel.

Company Captain Yorshka is speculated to be the daughter of Crossbreed Priscilla.

title: Ariamis
snippet: The Painted World of Ariamis was protected by an order of Painting Guardians. Anor Londo benefited from the Painted World as a prison for the spurned; it served as a place to seal away dangerous artifacts, abominations, sinners and Hollows. Velka, following from her role as the Goddess of Sin, eventually spread her influence inside the Painted World, where dozens of her cultist followers found refuge. Crossbreed Priscilla considered herself a guardian of the Painted World which she characterized as "peaceful". She pitied the "kind" inhabitants of the painting, as the outside world had shunned and locked them away, like herself. Priscilla became the "Lady" of the Painted World and its inhabitants, and welcomed the forlorn who were led into the cold world by the heretical tales of corvian storytellers. The humanoid corvians who found refuge in the Painting formed a small village, complete with knights and a library.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - the_painted_world_of_ariandel 
 the_painted_world_of_ariandel : Within the Cathedral of the Deep the Ashen One can encounter Slave Knight Gael, a Slave Knight who seeks unkindled ash to aid his Lady. Gael presents the Ashen One with a fragment of the Painted World of Ariandel, which sucks the Ashen One in. Within the painting, the Ashen One encounters Sister Friede and her loyal knight Sir Vilhelm. Friede is an advisor to Ariandel, the painting's creator, and convinced him to allow the painting to rot rather than allow it to be destroyed and replaced by a new one, despite the wishes of many of the painting's denizens. Friede bids the Ashen One to leave, telling them that they do not belong in the Painted World.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: location : The boss fight is found in an optional location of the Painted World of Ariandel. The player must destroy the rickety bridge that leads to the chapel from the side of said chapel, which will then allow them to climb down using the bridge's remains, like in the Catacombs of Carthus. From there, they must descend using the large roots jutting out of the cliffside, fending off Farron Followers and avoiding the exploding arrows that are shot by the two Millwood Knights below. After reaching the bottom, one can find the Depths of the Painting bonfire by proceeding forward from the last root where one of the Millwood Knights stood. From there, the boss fight can be reached by turning right and dropping down into the flower field opposite from the side of the frozen lake with Frost Crabs. The Champion's Gravetender will be found beneath a building resembling Crossbreed Priscilla's old battle arena from *Dark Souls*.

title: Large Leather Shield
snippet:
Large Leather Shield -  Dark Souls - shield - availability 
 availability : The Large Leather Shield is given to the Hunter class at the beginning of the game. It can also be purchased from Andre of Astora for 800 souls, or obtained as a drop from the Phalanx in the Painted World of Ariamis.

title: Bonfire (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Bonfire (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - painted_world_of_ariandel 
 painted_world_of_ariandel : ***Snowfield**
:The first bonfire available to the player in the Painted World. It is found directly outside the cave to which the player is teleported after speaking with Slave Knight Gael at the Cathedral of the Deep's Cleansing Chapel bonfire.

***Rope Bridge Cave**
:From the Snowfield bonfire, traveling north then east brings the player to an area populated by Farron Followers and wolves. Once the player has climbed the large hill to the north, and subsequently descended upon the other side, the Rope Bridge Cave bonfire can be found near the long rope bridge, in a cave along the right-hand cliff face. This small cave can be entered either from the front, or from a hole in its roof.

title: Black Set (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Black Set (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - availability 
 availability : The Black Set can be pillaged off a corpse in the Annex portion of the Painted World of Ariamis, hanging from a collapsed wall on the exterior side of the central decayed tower. It can most easily be accessed after finding the Annex Key, although it is possible to reach it without the key.

title: Soul of Priscilla
snippet:
Soul of Priscilla -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Soul of Priscilla the Crossbreed, trapped inside the painted world of Ariamis.

Special beings have special souls.

Use the soul of this crossbreed bastard child and antithesis to all life to acquire a huge amount of souls, or to create a unique weapon.

title: Skeleton
snippet:
Skeleton -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : Bonewheel Skeletons are distinct enemies, and can be encountered in the Painted World of Ariamis.
On rare occasions, when parried by a skeleton, a glitch may occur that sends the player falling through the ground.
Despite dropping the Red & White Round Shield, skeletons only wield the Warrior's Round Shield.
